src.q: Each tablet contains 10 mg of ezetimibe.
Each tablet contains 55 mg of lactose monohydrate.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Primary (heterozygous familial and non-familial) hypercholesterolaemia: with a statin when a statin alone is not enough, or alone when a statin is inappropriate or not tolerated; adjunct to diet.

src.q: who are not appropriately controlled with a statin alone
in whom a statin is considered inappropriate or is not tolerated

items.t: To reduce cardiovascular events in coronary heart disease with a history of acute coronary syndrome, added to or started with a statin. Also homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (with a statin) and homozygous sitosterolaemia.

src.q: patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) and a history of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) when added to ongoing statin therapy or initiated concomitantly with a statin
is indicated as adjunctive therapy to diet for use in patients with homozygous familial sitosterolaemia

items.t: Children: treatment must be started under specialist review.

src.q: Initiation of treatment must be performed under review of a specialist.

items.t: Adults: 10 mg once daily, at any time of day, with or without food. When added to a statin, continue the statin's usual starting dose or the established higher dose.

src.q: The recommended dose is one Ezetrol 10 mg tablet daily.
When Ezetrol is added to a statin, either the indicated usual initial dose of that particular statin or the already established higher statin dose should be continued.

items.t: With a bile acid sequestrant: take ezetimibe at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after it.

src.q: Dosing of Ezetrol should occur either ≥ 2 hours before or ≥ 4 hours after administration of a bile acid sequestrant.

items.t: Elderly and renal impairment: no dose adjustment. Mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh 5-6): no adjustment.

src.q: No dosage adjustment is required for elderly patients
No dosage adjustment is required for renally impaired patients
No dosage adjustment is required in patients with mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score 5 to 6).

items.t: Safety and efficacy at 6-17 years not established; no dose recommendation can be made. Not established under 6 years (no data). Specialist initiation.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of ezetimibe in children aged 6 to 17 years has not been established.
no recommendation on a posology can be made
The safety and efficacy of Ezetimibe in children aged < 6 years has not been established. No data are available.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to ezetimibe or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: With a statin: contraindicated in pregnancy and breastfeeding, and in active liver disease or unexplained persistent raised transaminases. Check the statin's own SmPC.

src.q: Therapy with Ezetrol co-administered with a statin is contraindicated during pregnancy and lactation.
Ezetrol co-administered with a statin is contraindicated in patients with active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations in serum transaminases.

items.t: Muscle: myopathy and rhabdomyolysis reported, mostly with a statin. If myopathy is suspected or CPK >10 x ULN, stop ezetimibe, any statin and other such agents at once.

src.q: Most patients who developed rhabdomyolysis were taking a statin concomitantly with Ezetrol.

If myopathy is suspected based on muscle symptoms or is confirmed by a creatine phosphokinase (CPK) level > 10 times the ULN, Ezetrol, any statin, and any of these other agents that the patient is taking concomitantly should be immediately discontinued.

items.t: Liver: with a statin, check liver function at the start and as the statin requires. Not recommended in moderate or severe hepatic impairment.

src.q: When Ezetrol is co-administered with a statin, liver function tests should be performed at initiation of therapy and according to the recommendations of the statin
Due to the unknown effects of the increased exposure to ezetimibe in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment, Ezetrol is not recommended

items.t: Fibrates: safety not established. With fenofibrate, investigate and stop if gallstones are suspected.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Ezetrol administered with fibrates have not been established.
If cholelithiasis is suspected in a patient receiving Ezetrol and fenofibrate, gallbladder investigations are indicated and this therapy should be discontinued

items.t: Contains lactose: patients with hereditary galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: Warfarin (or other coumarins, fluindione): increased INR reported after adding ezetimibe. Monitor INR.

src.q: there have been post-marketing reports of increased International Normalised Ratio (INR) in patients who had Ezetrol added to warfarin or fluindione
If Ezetrol is added to warfarin, another coumarin anticoagulant, or fluindione, INR should be appropriately monitored

items.t: Fenofibrate: possible risk of gallstones and gallbladder disease; investigate and stop if suspected. Fenofibrate raises ezetimibe levels about 1.5-fold.

src.q: In patients receiving fenofibrate and Ezetrol, physicians should be aware of the possible risk of cholelithiasis and gallbladder disease
Concomitant fenofibrate or gemfibrozil administration modestly increased total ezetimibe concentrations (approximately 1.5- and 1.7-fold respectively).

items.t: Statins: no clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction (rosuvastatin, atorvastatin, simvastatin and others). Muscle effects: see the statin SmPC.

src.q: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic interactions were seen when ezetimibe was co-administered with atorvastatin, simvastatin, pravastatin, lovastatin, fluvastatin, or rosuvastatin.

items.t: Ciclosporin: ezetimibe exposure rises markedly; caution when starting, and monitor ciclosporin levels. Cholestyramine lowers ezetimibe exposure by about 55%.

src.q: Caution should be exercised when initiating Ezetrol in the setting of ciclosporin. Ciclosporin concentrations should be monitored in patients receiving Ezetrol and ciclosporin
Concomitant cholestyramine administration decreased the mean area under the curve (AUC) of total ezetimibe (ezetimibe + ezetimibe-glucuronide) approximately 55 %.

items.t: Antacids slow absorption but this is not clinically significant.

src.q: This decreased rate of absorption is not considered clinically significant.

items.t: No dose adjustment in renal impairment.

src.q: No dosage adjustment is required for renally impaired patients

items.t: Mild (Child-Pugh 5-6): no adjustment. Moderate (Child-Pugh 7-9) or severe (Child-Pugh >9): not recommended. With a statin: contraindicated in active liver disease.

src.q: Treatment with Ezetrol is not recommended in patients with moderate (Child-Pugh score 7 to 9) or severe (Child-Pugh score > 9) liver dysfunction

items.t: With a statin: contraindicated. Alone: give only if clearly necessary (no human data). No BUMPS leaflet for ezetimibe was found.

src.q: Therapy with Ezetrol co-administered with a statin is contraindicated during pregnancy and lactation.
Ezetrol should be given to pregnant women only if clearly necessary.

items.t: SmPC: should not be used during breastfeeding (and contraindicated with a statin).

src.q: Ezetrol should not be used during lactation.

items.t: SPS (differs from SmPC): can be used with caution with infant monitoring, but statins are preferred. Monitor infant feeding, growth and weight, and for diarrhoea, abdominal pain, flatulence, lethargy and irritability.

src.q: Ezetimibe can be used with caution and infant monitoring during breastfeeding, but statins are preferred.
Also monitor the infant for potential side effects including diarrhoea, abdominal pain, flatulence, lethargy and irritability.

items.t: No human fertility data; no effect on fertility in rats.

src.q: No clinical trial data are available on the effects of ezetimibe on human fertility.

items.t: Common: headache, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, flatulence, myalgia, fatigue, raised ALT and/or AST. With fenofibrate: abdominal pain (common).

src.q: Nervous system disorders Common headache
Gastrointestinal disorders Common abdominal pain; diarrhoea; flatulence
Common myalgia
Common fatigue
Common ALT and/or AST increased

items.t: Myopathy/rhabdomyolysis (frequency not known): stop at once if suspected or CPK >10 x ULN.

src.q: Not known myopathy/rhabdomyolysis
Ezetrol, any statin, and any of these other agents that the patient is taking concomitantly should be immediately discontinued

items.t: Frequency not known: anaphylaxis and angio-oedema, hepatitis, gallstones, cholecystitis, pancreatitis, thrombocytopenia, erythema multiforme.

src.q: Not known hypersensitivity; including rash; urticaria; anaphylaxis and angio-oedema
Not known hepatitis; cholelithiasis; cholecystitis
Not known pancreatitis; constipation

items.t: With a statin: liver function tests at the start and then as advised for the statin.

src.q: When Ezetrol is co-administered with a statin, liver function tests should be performed at initiation of therapy and according to the recommendations of the statin

items.t: INR when ezetimibe is added to warfarin.

src.q: If Ezetrol is added to warfarin, another coumarin anticoagulant, or fluindione, the International Normalised Ratio (INR) should be appropriately monitored

items.t: Stop ezetimibe (and any statin) if myopathy is suspected or CPK >10 x ULN.

src.q: If myopathy is suspected based on muscle symptoms or is confirmed by a creatine phosphokinase (CPK) level > 10 times the ULN

items.t: Oral, once daily at any time of day, with or without food. Stay on a lipid-lowering diet.

src.q: Ezetrol can be administered at any time of the day, with or without food.
The patient should be on an appropriate lipid-lowering diet and should continue on this diet during treatment with Ezetrol.

items.t: Report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness promptly.

src.q: All patients starting therapy with Ezetrol should be advised of the risk of myopathy and told to report promptly any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness

items.t: Dizziness has been reported; take this into account when driving.

src.q: when driving vehicles or operating machines, it should be taken into account that dizziness has been reported
Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

rules.concern: With a statin only: active liver disease or unexplained persistent raised transaminases
rules.consequence: Listed in SmPC section 4.3 for use with a statin. Alone: not recommended in moderate or severe hepatic impairment.
rules.action: Do not use ezetimibe together with a statin. Ezetimibe alone: not recommended in moderate or severe hepatic impairment.

src.q: Ezetrol co-administered with a statin is contraindicated in patients with active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations in serum transaminases.
Treatment with Ezetrol is not recommended in patients with moderate (Child-Pugh score 7 to 9) or severe (Child-Pugh score > 9) liver dysfunction

rules.consequence: Increased INR reported after adding ezetimibe.

src.q: there have been post-marketing reports of increased International Normalised Ratio (INR) in patients who had Ezetrol added to warfarin or fluindione
If Ezetrol is added to warfarin, another coumarin anticoagulant, or fluindione, INR should be appropriately monitored

rules.consequence: Possible risk of gallstones and gallbladder disease; ezetimibe levels rise about 1.5-fold. Safety with fibrates not established.
rules.action: Be aware of the risk; if gallstones are suspected, investigate the gallbladder and stop this therapy.
rules.sourceWording: physicians should be aware of the possible risk

If cholelithiasis is suspected in a patient receiving Ezetrol and fenofibrate, gallbladder investigations are indicated and this therapy should be discontinued

rules.consequence: Most rhabdomyolysis cases with ezetimibe were in patients also taking a statin. With a statin: contraindicated in pregnancy, breastfeeding and active liver disease.
rules.action: Warn about muscle symptoms; stop ezetimibe and the statin at once if myopathy is suspected or CPK >10 x ULN. Check liver function at the start.

src.q: Most patients who developed rhabdomyolysis were taking a statin concomitantly with Ezetrol.

If myopathy is suspected based on muscle symptoms or is confirmed by a creatine phosphokinase (CPK) level > 10 times the ULN, Ezetrol, any statin, and any of these other agents that the patient is taking concomitantly should be immediately discontinued.

rules.consequence: No clinical data. With a statin the combination is contraindicated (SmPC 4.3).
